name: Serpentine Belt
summary: Upgraded from BLOCKED. The BMW ETK diagram 'Belt drive - generator/AC/power steering' (RealOEM decode of this VIN's tail: E90 LCI 328i sedan, N52N, built 09/2009, US) settles the part-number conflicts: ribbed V-belt 6PK1990 = 11287628650 (older numbers 11287549150/11287527564 are previous revisions per Turner), mechanical belt tensioner = 11288624196 with M11x65 ALUMINIUM Torx screw 11287530315 ('aluminium screws may only be used once'), deflection pulley 11287535860, protective caps 11287535867 and 11281435114. Engine is N52N per ETK; the same belt number is listed by a retailer for N51, N52N and N53 so N51-vs-N52 no longer matters for the belt. Two independent secondary procedures (FCP Euro N52 article; Pelican Parts E90 article) agree on T60 tensioner release rotating clockwise and removing intake ducting/airbox (and fan shroud on one) first. Tensioner bolt torque 25 Nm + 90 degrees is corroborated by FCP plus four forum sources but NO BMW document (VERIFIED_SECONDARY, primary:false). Idler (deflection) pulley bolt torque is CONFLICT (40 Nm vs 80 Nm) and must not be published. Pass 2: the ETK diagram carries no engine/transmission/option condition, bimmerworld lists the same tensioner for N51/N52 and a retailer lists the same belt for N51/N52N/N53, so engine label (RealOEM N52N vs N52K from VIN decoders) does not change any part or step. A/C compressor is on this belt with no option split in the ETK. Transmission: the owner states automatic, so the FCP T25 transmission-oil-cooler fastener on the fan shroud applies (single source). Correction: bimmerpost thread p=19426657 is an N54 335i thread and is no longer counted for N52 idler torque or access. Bentley published an erratum for the N52/N52KP idler-pulley-to-alternator torque, which explains why 40 vs 80 Nm disagree; the idler torque stays CONFLICT and unpublished. Still missing: lock-pin diameter and whether the pin exists on this tensioner, a belt routing diagram, alternator pulley torque, the BMW repair instruction, E14 size confirmation (single source). Usable as an uncertified draft: belt/tensioner/pulley parts, tools, release direction, tensioner bolt (secondary 25 Nm + 90 deg) and step order are supported; idler bolt torque must be left out and the routing must be photographed before removal.
variantDependencies: Engine label: RealOEM VIN-tail decode (A175760, E90 LCI 328i, 09/2009, PH73 USA) = N52N; VIN decoders cited elsewhere (bimmer.work, a bimmerpost poster with a 2009 328i) say N52K. These are different naming schemes for the same 3.0 L N52B30 family (BMW's September 2006 N52 revision is called N52KP/N52K); NHTSA vPIC gives displacement 3.0 L, 6 cyl and no engine model. No source shows a belt, tensioner or pulley difference between the labels: ETK diagram 11_3740 has no engine condition and Bentley's N52/N52KP erratum treats both as one family. Label stays UNRESOLVED as a name but is not a procedure variable. [https://www.realoem.com/bmw/enUS/select?vin=A175760] [https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeVinValues/WBAPH7C58AA175760?format=json&modelyear=2010] [https://bentleypubs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/tech/pages/437454449/121-20+N52+engine%2C+Idler+pulley+to+alternator+housing+torque+correction]

N51 (SULEV) vs N52: RealOEM decodes this VIN tail as N52N, not N51, so N51 is excluded by the catalog decode. Even if it were an N51, bimmerworld lists the same 11288624196 tensioner for N51/N52 and a retailer lists the same belt for N51/N52N/N53; Turner says N51 and N52 look identical and the SULEV label under the hood is the identifier. [https://www.bimmerworld.com/Engine/Pulleys/BMW-MECHANICAL-BELT-TENSIONER-11287530314-11288624196.html] [https://www.turnermotorsport.com/t-E90_SULEV_N51_or_LEV_N52]

Transmission: owner states automatic (RealOEM decode does not show it). FCP: automatic cars have an external transmission oil cooler on the fan shroud held by one T25 fastener that must come off before the shroud (single source). Applies to this car if the fan shroud is removed; not needed if the shroud stays on. Manual-only branch not applicable.
Drive: owner states rear-wheel drive (PH73 type code); xDrive not applicable. No source shows a belt difference for xDrive on E90 LCI.

A/C and power steering: ETK diagram 11_3740 is titled generator/AC/power steering and lists one belt, one tensioner, one deflection pulley with no option or market condition, so the A/C compressor and the power steering pump are on this belt on this car. Turner notes exclusions only for X5 with Adaptive Drive/4-zone climate (not E90).
Alternator pulley removal may need a special tool (BimmerWorld CTA-8088 for Bosch alternators); only if the alternator pulley itself is being replaced.

Access path differs by source: FCP removes snorkel, airbox and fan shroud; Pelican removes the front intake duct, a duct across the radiator and a 6 mm Allen fastener and raises the front of the car; a 2008 528i poster says fan shroud and intake housing removal makes the work easier. Both approaches are presented; which one is needed depends on tool clearance.

Tensioner lock pin: FCP (N52 article) says pull the pin after routing; Pelican staff say none is used; an N55 thread says the pin must be removed first. Whether the 11288624196 tensioner is supplied with a pin is not established; handled as a branch in step 9.

tools.note: Two independent step-by-step articles; also a 5series poster mentions a large Torx/T50 uncertainly. Schwaben N54 tool uses T60 head.

tools.item: E14 external Torx socket (tensioner mounting bolt)
tools.note: Single source. ETK and BimmerWorld call the part a 'Torx screw' M11x65 without saying internal or external Torx, so E14 external is neither confirmed nor contradicted; test-fit and do not force.

tools.item: T25 socket (fan shroud, transmission oil cooler fastener), 10 mm socket (airbox bolts)
tools.note: FCP: automatic cars have a transmission oil cooler on the fan shroud held by one T25 fastener; this car is automatic (owner-stated), so it applies only if the shroud is removed.

tools.item: T20 Torx (intake duct) and 6 mm Allen (duct fastener)
Torque wrench (low range) plus angle gauge/protractor for the 90 degree step
Small flat screwdriver (pulley caps, hose clamp, connector tabs, duct tabs)
Alternator pulley removal tool (CTA-8088 for Bosch alternators) - only if replacing the alternator pulley

tools.note: FCP says to pull the lock pin after routing the belt; Pelican staff say no pin is needed; an N55 thread (other engine) says the pin must come out before belt install. Pin diameter and presence on this tensioner not given anywhere. Not resolvable remotely; handled as a branch in step 9.

torque.conflicts: 40 Nm vs 80 Nm (vs an unanswered 19 Nm question). Bentley Publishers' B310 E90 manual update '121-20 N52 engine, Idler pulley to alternator housing torque correction' (2015, applies to N52/N52KP) shows the printed BMW-derived value was wrong and was corrected, but the corrected number is not readable. The earlier N54 bimmerpost '38 Nm pulleys' figure is from a 335i thread and is excluded. Do not publish a number until a BMW repair instruction or the Bentley corrected table is read.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Work on a cool engine with the key out. Note that the aluminium tensioner bolt is single-use and the tensioner spring is strong.
warnings: Keep hands, hair and clothing clear of belt and fan.
Tensioner is under considerable spring force; do not release it uncontrolled.

steps.title: Clear access to the belt
steps.instruction: Remove the air intake snorkel/duct and airbox (FCP: snorkel two fasteners, airbox two 10 mm bolts, hose clamp, MAF connector). Pelican alternative: two T20 at the front duct, loosen clamp and turn the hose lock 90 degrees, remove the 6 mm Allen fastener and raise the front. Remove the fan assembly if you need room for the tool (FCP: unplug the connector, free the expansion tank line, T25 at the shroud top; automatics also have a T25 oil-cooler fastener). This car is an automatic (owner-stated), so if the fan shroud comes out, expect the extra T25 oil-cooler fastener; skip it if the shroud stays on.
warnings: Unplug the MAF sensor cleanly; do not strain connectors.
Fan shroud fits tightly; wiggle it clear.
steps.sourcesNote: Both approaches documented; which is needed depends on tool and fan clearance. The N54 bimmerpost thread formerly cited here was removed.

steps.title: Record belt path
steps.instruction: Photograph or sketch the belt path and note direction of rotation before removing anything; this is mandatory because no routing diagram could be read remotely. The order given is crank, A/C compressor, power steering pump, idler, alternator, tensioner (Pelican); ETK confirms those same components share one 6PK1990 belt.
warnings: If photos and the new belt do not match, stop; routing differs by model per Pelican staff.

steps.title: Release the tensioner and take the belt off
steps.instruction: Fit a T60 on a long-handled ratchet in the tensioner release point, rotate clockwise and hold, lift the belt off the tensioner pulley, then off the other pulleys.
warnings: Release slowly; keep fingers out of the belt path; a slipping bit can injure.
Do not use an undersized tool.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.instruction: Fold the belt to check rib cracks, glazing and chunks; spin the idler and tensioner pulleys for play, rough rotation or noise; replace worn parts. Replace the tensioner together with the belt when it is worn. If the idler pulley is worn or noisy, do not replace it from this guide (the idler step is blocked): have a BMW-qualified shop do it.

steps.title: Replace the idler pulley (optional)
steps.instruction: Pry off the idler caps with a flat screwdriver, remove the 16 mm deep-socket bolt that holds the pulley to the alternator, fit the new pulley by hand to avoid cross-threading, reinstall caps. Torque is NOT publishable (40 Nm vs 80 Nm conflict).
warnings: Do not guess the torque; use BMW repair data.

steps.title: Replace the tensioner (optional)
steps.instruction: Remove the single E14 mounting bolt and the tensioner. Fit the new tensioner with a NEW single-use aluminium M11x65 bolt: thread by hand, torque 25 Nm then a further 90 degrees. Remove any retaining disc on the back of the new pulley if the kit instructs (E82 post).
warnings: Aluminium bolt may only be used once (ETK).
Never reuse the bolt; torque + angle figure is from secondary sources, not a BMW document.

steps.title: Route the new belt
steps.instruction: Use the 6PK1990 belt 11287628650. Seat it on the crank pulley first (slide in sideways), then A/C compressor, power steering pump, idler and alternator, and finally onto the tensioner pulley while the T60 holds tension released. Check every rib is in its groove.
warnings: A mis-seated belt can jump off or shred.

steps.title: Apply tension
steps.instruction: Let the tensioner back slowly. Branch: if the tensioner carries a lock pin (FCP: pull it only after the belt is routed; an N55 thread says the pin must be out before the belt goes on), follow the pin that is actually fitted; if there is no pin (Pelican staff), just rotate and release. Re-check seating on every pulley.
warnings: Pin size and location not documented; Pelican says no pin is used.

steps.title: Reassemble
steps.instruction: Refit the fan assembly (reconnect plug, expansion line, T25, new zip tie for wiring), airbox/ducting and intake snorkel; reconnect the MAF sensor.
warnings: Torque values for these fasteners not sourced; snug only.

steps.title: Verify
steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it run briefly, shut off and recheck belt alignment on all pulleys; then run again and check noise and charging.
warnings: If the belt walks off or squeals, stop and re-inspect pulleys/tensioner.

safety: Engine cold, key out; keep hands and hair clear of belt, fans and pulleys.
Tensioner is under strong spring pressure; release with the correct T60 and long handle and hold it controlled.
Aluminium tensioner bolt is single-use; replace every time it is removed.
Do not publish or rely on the idler pulley torque until conflict resolved.
Torque + angle figures come from secondary sources only; verify with BMW repair data when possible.

Never work under, or take a wheel off, a car held only by a jack. Support it on rated jack stands on hard, level ground, or use a lift or drive-on ramps where the job allows. Use the jacking points shown in the jacking illustration in your owner's manual, with a pad or adapter between the jack and the plastic pad. If you cannot identify a safe place for the stand from your manual, stop and use a shop lift.

CHECKED 2026-10-11 (NOT RESOLVED): a research-report claim that the 40 Nm and 80 Nm figures belong to different components (alternator pulley vs idler) was tested against the primary pages. FCP Euro's N52 article names 40 Nm as the IDLER pulley bolt (the pulley that bolts to the alternator) and gives 25 Nm + 90 degrees for the tensioner bolt; it lists no separate alternator-pulley torque.
